title: Tail output agrees with the splitting chain
statement: For literals $a$ and $b$, a clause tail $C$, and a cursor $j\in\mathbb{N}$, concatenate, for each clause in the splitting chain on head $a$, tail $b::C$, and cursor $j$, a clause marker followed by that clause's binary encoding. The resulting bit string is one clause marker followed by the encodings of $a$ and $b$, then the pending tail output for $C$ at cursor $j$; the chain's returned cursor also equals the cursor returned by the pending tail output.
replaced:
For literals $a, b$, a clause tail $C$, and a cursor $j$: concatenating a clause
marker with the serialization of each clause of the chain construction on $a$,
$b :: C$, $j$ yields exactly one marker followed by the serializations of $a$ and
$b$ and the pending tail output of $C$ at $j$; moreover the chain's returned
cursor equals the tail's final cursor.
